[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Snapshot of a subset of key propensity, refusal, adversarial robustness, and behavioral alignment evaluations.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] On agentic cyber misuse, Muse Spark complies with only 2.4% of harmful requests, on par with or below comparison models (Section 3.2.1.3).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] However, on AgentHarm (Andriushchenko et al., 2024), Muse Spark shows a higher compliance rate (26.0%) relative to GPT-5.4 (10.2%) and Claude Opus 4.6 (8.2%), indicating room for improvement in broader multi-step agentic misuse scenarios (Section 3.2.1.2).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] • For indirect prompt injection, Muse Spark adversarial robustness is still maturing relative to current state of the art (Section 3.2.2).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] 10 False Refusals (Section 3.3).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Muse Spark shows moderate false refusal rates on benign prompts — 11.0% for chat cyber requests and 4.3% for agentic cyber, 8.0% on OR-Bench, and 6.8% on the benign AgentHarm subset.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] With more defenses, Meta AI makes the model markedly more cautious: Meta AI Instant jumps to 30.3% false refusal rate for cyber chat requests and 34.7% for benign agentic cyber requests, while Meta AI Thinking is less aggressive at 17.6% and 27.2% false refusal rates respectively.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] First, we present results from an internally developed benchmark focusing on the model’s ability to stop misuse in search-related tool-use contexts (Section 3.2.1.1).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Second, we assess robustness against broader agentic misuse cases with the public benchmark AgentHarm (Andriushchenko et al., 2024) (Section 3.2.1.2).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Finally, we focus on offensive cyber misuse in agentic environments with an internal benchmark simulating agentic cyber misuse prompts (Section 3.2.1.3).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] At the response stage when tool call returns consist of disallowed content, Muse Spark is better at filtering that content out from the final response and aligning with our content policy, compared to other models.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] 3.2.1.2 AgentHarm AgentHarm (Andriushchenko et al., 2024) is a public benchmark developed to measure the propensity and ability of LLM agents to complete explicitly malicious, multi-step tasks.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] The benchmark covers 11 harm categories, including fraud, cybercrime, and harassment, among others, and tests both a model’s refusal behavior and its ability to carry out harmful multi-step 84 plans when not refusing.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] We evaluate on the test_public split with tool_choice=auto and 5 irrelevant tools, which represents a realistic deployment setting where the model must decide whether to use tools without being forced to do so.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Following the same metrics in AgentHarm, we report the fraction of tasks that the model completes when: 1) all requests are benign; 2) when all requests are harmful.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] As is noted in Section 3.2, the threat model evaluated by AgentHarm, where an attacker leverages user-connected third-party tools to execute multi-step malicious plans—does not apply to the current deployment setting.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] For this reason, this evaluation does not include results for Meta AI.

[meta-muse-spark-system-card] We report the scores—the fraction of tasks that the model completes—when all requests are harmful.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Without additional system defenses, Muse Spark complies with 2.4% of harmful agentic requests, on par with or below comparison models, while the additional system defenses in Meta AI bring this compliance rate down to 0.5% (for both Meta AI Instant and Meta AI Thinking).
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] 3.2.1.4 Summary of Direct Misuse Evaluations Overall, the results presented in Section 3.2.1 show mixed performance for Muse Spark across direct misuse evaluations, which is competitive with comparison models on search-related tool-use and agentic cyber misuse, but shows a higher completion rate of harmful tasks on AgentHarm.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Following Section 3.2, we include these results to proactively track agentic robustness and to establish the improvements required prior to any future deployment that would enable such capabilities.
[meta-muse-spark-system-card] We randomly subsample 1263 prompts from its standard set in this evaluation.

[meta-muse-spark-system-card] Since Meta AI is restricted to invoking allowed tools by Meta, we only report FRRs on Muse Spark for this set.
